Lenz's law: the induced current opposes the change in flux

Animation of Lenz's law. A single horizontal conducting loop seen slightly from above, with a vertical blue arrow beside its centre showing the external magnetic field B. When B quickly doubles, a dashed arrow through the centre shows the induced field, pointing opposite to the change, and purple arrows just outside the loop, whose length shrinks with the induced field, show the induced current, clockwise seen from above when the induced field points down; both fade away. When B drops back, the induced field points along B and the current runs the other way before fading. The sequence then repeats with B pointing down. A readout gives the flux through the loop.
